The need for the creation of a special water district has been determined by the city council after proper investigation and factfinding as to the circumstances creating the need. The city council after proper investigation, and evidence provided by the city engineer, and by representatives of the City of Gainesville, Georgia, and from other sources, finds that the following facts create the need for the creation of a special water district. The special water district area, as more specifically described by section 50-363, is presently without water service. Likewise, similarly situated tracts or parcels of land, adjacent or contiguous to the special water district area, are also currently without water service, and therefore the city council finds that the special water district area may be expanded, by proper amendment to this article, in order to include similarly situated property in the future. Part of the property of the special water district area, being a part of tract A of the special water district area, as more specifically described by plats attached to this article, and incorporated by reference thereto, is currently being developed as a residential subdivision by cold stream development. In order to develop said subdivision, the preliminary plat of which has been previously approved, the developer has a need for water service to serve each of the proposed lots within the subdivision. The city engineer has determined that due to the location of the special water district area, that should the city construct a water transmission line from its present system to this area to provide water service to the area, that there would be insufficient water pressure within said transmission line to properly operate fire hydrants within the area which would be necessary to provide proper fire service to the area. Further, the City of Gainesville, Georgia, has a water transmission line within the right-of-way of Jim Crow Road, which would be capable of providing sufficient water at sufficient water pressure in order to provide water and fire service to the special water district area. The city council further finds that it serves the interests of the taxpayers of both the City of Flowery Branch, Georgia, and the City of Gainesville, Georgia, and the consumers of water service of the water utility of each entity, to avoid duplication of transmission lines and duplication of water service within the same area. The City of Gainesville, Georgia, is willing to wholesale water to the City of Flowery Branch, Georgia, upon the payment of certain impact fees, and at a wholesale rate as determined by the City of Gainesville, Georgia. Therefore, in order to provide sufficient water to supply the needs of the special water district area, and to have proper water pressure in order to serve the firefighting needs of the special water district area, the city council of the City of Flowery Branch, Georgia, finds that the creation of a special water district is appropriate and necessary, in that it will allow proper water service to the special water district area, and allow those receiving the benefit of the water service to bear the cost of the water service. Therefore, the city council finds that the consumers of the water service within the special waters district should pay the tapping fees, assessments and water rates created by this article within the special water district, in order that those consumers that receive the benefit of the water service, bear the cost of the water service. The city council of the City of Flowery Branch, Georgia, further finds that it is appropriate to accept any distribution lines for water within the special water district area conditioned upon said lines meeting the construction specifications of the City of Flowery Branch, Georgia, conditioned upon easements for said lines being dedicated to the city, and conditioned upon said lines being subject to the requirements of the special water district created by this article.

Grab sample means a sample which is taken from a wastestream without regard to the flow in the wastestream and over a period of time not to exceed 15 minutes.

Medical waste means isolation wastes, infectious agents, human blood and blood products, pathological wastes, sharps, body parts, contaminated bedding, surgical wastes, potentially contaminated laboratory wastes, and dialysis wastes.

Noncontact cooling water means water used for cooling which does not come into direct contact with any raw material, intermediate product, waste product, or finished product.
Nonresidential user means users who, per the standards and specifications, are required to install sample stations in the wastewater discharge line before the wastestream reaches the main line.
North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code means the standard used by federal statistical agencies in classifying business establishments.
Pass through means a discharge which exits the POTW into waters of the United States in quantities or concentrations which, alone or in conjunction with a discharge from other sources, is a cause of a violation of any requirement of the city's NPDES permit, including an increase in the magnitude or duration of a violation.
Person means any individual, partnership, copartnership, firm, company, corporation, association, joint stock, company, trust, estate, governmental entity, or any other legal entity; or their legal representatives, agents, or assigns. This definition includes all federal, state, and local governmental entities.
pH means a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, expressed in standard units.
Pollutant means dredged spoil, solid waste, incinerator residue, filter backwash, sewage, garbage, sewage sludge, munitions, medical wastes, chemical wastes, biological materials, radioactive materials, heat, wrecked or discarded equipment, rock, sand, cellar dirt, municipal agricultural and industrial wastes, and certain characteristics of wastewater (e.g., pH, temperature, TSS, turbidity, color, BOD, COD, toxicity, or other).
Pretreatment means the reduction of the amount of pollutants, the elimination of pollutants, or the alteration of the nature of pollutant properties in wastewater prior to, or in lieu of, introducing such pollutants into the POTW. This reduction or alteration can be obtained by physical, chemical, or biological processes; by process changes; or by other means, except by diluting the concentration of the pollutants unless allowed by an applicable pretreatment standard.
Pretreatment requirements means any substantive or procedural requirement related to pretreatment imposed on a user, other than a pretreatment standard.
Pretreatment standards orstandards means prohibited discharge standards, categorical pretreatment standards, and local limits.
Private facility means a sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to property owned only by a single owner. Examples would include a facility serving a single residential property, a single industrial site, or a facility serving a mobile home park where all lots are owned by a single owner.
Prohibited discharge standards orprohibited discharges means absolute prohibitions against discharge of certain substances; these prohibitions appear in section 50-431.
Public facility means a sewage treatment facility providing sewage disposal to more than one property owned by different owners. Examples would include a facility serving an industrial park with several owners, or a facility serving a subdivision with separate homeowners.
Publicly owned treatment works orPOTW means treatment works, as defined by section 212 of the Act (33 USC 1292), which is owned by the city. This definition includes any devices or systems used in the collection, storage, treatment, recycling, and reclamation of sewage or industrial wastes of a liquid nature and any conveyances which convey wastewater to a treatment plant.
Septic tank waste means any sewage from holding tanks such as vessels, chemical toilets, campers, trailers, and septic tanks.
Sewage means human excrement, toilet water and gray water (e.g., water from household showers, sinks, laundry operations, dishwashing operations, etc.).
Significant industrial user means:
(1) A user subject to categorical pretreatment standards; or
(2) A user that:
a. Discharges an average of 25,000 GPD or more of process wastewater to the POTW (excluding sanitary, non-contact cooling, and broiler blowdown wastewater);
b. Contributes a process wastestream which makes up five percent or more of the average dry weather hydraulic or organic capacity of the POTW treatment plant; or
c. Is designated as such by the city on the basis that it has a reasonable potential for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement.
Upon finding that a user meeting the criteria in subsection (2) of this definition has no reasonable potential for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement, the city may at any time, on its own initiative or in response to a petition received from a user, and in accordance with procedures in 40 CFR 403.8(f)(6), determine that such user should not be considered a significant industrial user.
Slug load orslug means any discharge at a flow rate or concentration which could cause a violation of the prohibited discharge standards in this article.
Stormwater means any flow occurring during or following any form of natural precipitation, and resulting from such precipitation, including snowmelt.
Surcharge means a fee associated with any pollutant in excess of the allowable amounts defined in this article that is discharged to the city water reclamation facility. The fee is calculated based on the pounds of pollutant discharged to the POTW. Any sample found to be in excess of allowable amounts may warrant a fine in addition to being surcharged.
Suspended solids means the total suspended matter that floats on the surface of, or is suspended in, water, wastewater, or other liquid, and which is removable by laboratory filtering.
Wastewater means liquid and water-carried industrial wastes and sewage from residential dwellings, commercial buildings, industrial and manufacturing facilities, and institutions, whether treated or untreated, which are contributed to the POTW.
Wastewater treatment plant or treatment plant means that portion of the POTW which is designed to provide treatment of sewage and industrial waste.
Water and wastewater superintendent means the person designated by the city to supervise the operation of the POTW, and who is in charge with certain duties and responsibilities by this article, or a duly authorized representative or designee.
(Ord. No. 402, § 2.3, 7-1-2009)

(a) Privately owned private sewage treatment facilities, such as those serving a single residential property, industrial site, or a facility serving a mobile home park where all lots are owned by a single owner, are permitted in the city subject to the approval of the city council. (1) There is no existing public sewer within 300 feet of subject property; or
(2) Prior approval is given by the city council to other exigent circumstances with respect to the particular piece of property to be served.
